Here are the EXACT prompts I use to produce a full AI story video from idea to upload:

These are the prompts running behind $2M+ in channel revenue across my community, far beyond any generic "write me a YouTube script" request. Every prompt is designed for Claude Opus 5, and nearly all of them work with any frontier model.

STAGE 1: niche research prompt (Claude + NexLev MCP)

"Use NexLev MCP to find 10 YouTube channels in the [NICHE] space launched in the last 12 months with average views above 1,000 per video. Return the channel name, subscriber count, total videos, average views per video, estimated RPM range, primary audience demographic, and the titles of the top 3 outlier videos for each channel. Sort by average views descending."

This prompt pulls live YouTube data through NexLev's MCP integration. The output is a structured research report replacing 2-3 hours of manual tab-opening. You get channel-level performance data, outlier titles, and RPM estimates in one response.

STAGE 2: outlier analysis prompt

"Analyze the outlier video titles from the channels above. Identify 1) the most common emotional triggers used in high-performing titles, 2) the structural formulas repeated across outliers (e.G. [person] + [action] + [nation]), 3) which title lengths perform best, 4) whether broad titles outperform specific titles. Based on the patterns, generate 15 title ideas optimized for outlier performance in this niche."

Feed this to Claude right after the niche research prompt. The model analyzes the patterns across all the outlier titles and reverse-engineers the formula driving clicks. The 15 title ideas at the end are data-backed rather than creative guesses.

STAGE 3: script generation prompt

"You are a professional long-form narrative scriptwriter for YouTube AI story channels. Write a [LENGTH]-minute voiceover script about [TOPIC] using the following structure:

HOOK (first 30 seconds): open with a specific date, location, and character. Establish immediate tension or stakes. The viewer must know within 30 seconds why this story matters.

CONTEXT (minutes 1-5): establish the wider context, the stakes beyond the individual story, and introduce the key characters with ONE specific, memorable anecdote per character establishing personality and motivation.

RISING CONFLICT (minutes 5-15): build tension through escalating events. Each scene raises the stakes. Alternate between high-intensity and breathing room. Never maintain the same intensity for more than 3 minutes.

CLIMAX (minutes 15-18): deliver the payoff the hook promised. Use visceral, visual language. Make the viewer feel present in the moment.

RESOLUTION + LEGACY (minutes 18-20): connect the story's outcome to something bigger. Show why this event mattered beyond itself. End with a line worth remembering.

RULES: skip filler phrases entirely, drop the "welcome to the channel" opener, and don't use rhetorical questions as transitions. Every sentence earns the next one. Use specific numbers, dates, names, and locations throughout. The script must be factually accurate."

This is the core scripting prompt. The structure embedded in the prompt holds Claude to a retention-optimized narrative arc instead of rambling through information at a flat pace. The rules section eliminates the AI-isms (filler, rhetorical transitions, generic openers) before they appear.

Adjust [LENGTH] and the minute ranges to match your niche's optimal video length.

STAGE 4: image generation prompt

"Based on the following script, generate 20 image generation prompts for [IMAGE MODEL, e.G. NanoBanana Pro] producing super-realistic images depicting key moments from the story. Each prompt should specify character age, physical appearance (clothing, hair, expression, posture), setting (location, time of day, weather, architecture), lighting (direction, color temperature, mood), and camera angle (wide shot, medium, close-up). Maintain visual consistency by describing recurring characters with the same physical details in every prompt."

Paste the full script above this prompt. Claude reads the narrative and generates 20 scene-specific image prompts. The level of detail in the prompt ensures the image model receives enough visual direction to produce cinematic-quality output.

STAGE 5: thumbnail generation prompt

"I need a thumbnail image prompt for a YouTube video titled '[VIDEO TITLE]' in the [NICHE] niche. The thumbnail should 1) feature [NUMBER] characters with specific, exaggerated facial expressions conveying [EMOTION], 2) be set in [SETTING] with [LIGHTING CONDITIONS], 3) leave the top corners relatively uncluttered for title text overlay, 4) use [COLOR TEMPERATURE] tones matching the mood. Style reference: hyperrealistic cinematic film still, 16:9 horizontal, [GENRE DESCRIPTOR]. Include 8k detail, photorealistic skin texture, volumetric light, and shallow depth of field."

Send this along with a competitor thumbnail as a style reference. Claude generates a prompt specific to your video and niche. The "leave top corners uncluttered" instruction is critical because you need space for the text overlay doing the emotional selling.

STAGE 6: channel description prompt

"Rewrite the following YouTube channel description to sound professional, engaging, and niche-appropriate for a [NICHE] channel. Keep the tone [TONE: mysterious/authoritative/warm]. Include a brief hook explaining what the channel covers, a line on upload frequency, and a subtle call to subscribe. Under 150 words."

Paste a competitor's description below the prompt. Claude rewrites the description matching the tone of your specific niche. Use the output as your channel description AND your default video description.

STAGE 7: translation prompt (for secondary language channels)

"You are a professional literary translator and localizer for long-form narrative video scripts. Translate the script below from english into [TARGET LANGUAGE]. Rules: 1) translate 1:1, faithful and complete. Do not summarize, shorten, expand, or omit anything. 2) preserve the original meaning, tone, emotional register, narrative voice, pacing, and rhythm. Translate idioms and expressions into natural equivalents. 3) localize character names and place names into natural forms for [TARGET LANGUAGE]. Keep names 100% consistent throughout. 4) preserve exact formatting and paragraph structure. 5) output ONLY the translated script, with no preamble or notes attached."

Translation channels multiply your revenue with minimal extra work. One script, two languages, two revenue streams. This prompt ensures the translated version reads like a native script rather than a Google-translate artifact.

**Holding AI to the Truth: Why Blockchain Matters** (written with assistance from @Grok.  

Artificial intelligence is extraordinary at producing fluent answers. It is less reliable at producing *settled* ones. On occasion — more often than casual users admit — models *hallucinate*: they invent citations, invent facts, invent confidence. The output can look authoritative and still be wrong. That is not a moral failing of the machine; it is a property of probabilistic generation without a shared ledger of what actually happened.

In July 2019, on Real Vision with Raoul Pal (@RaoulGMI) macro investor Dan Tapiero (@DTAPCAP) named the other half of this problem years before “AI agents” entered every pitch deck. Bitcoin, he argued, is not merely a coin. It is an *invention* — and at its core, “a truth machine”: a system bought for “certainty, of confirmation, of validity, of security,” a platform with a track record that makes fraud and silent revision harder. He later sharpened the phrase to “security truth machine.” (Popular memory sometimes upgrades that to “automatic truth machine”; the idea is the same.)

The distinction that matters for AI is precise. A blockchain does not magically know whether a claim about the physical world is true. It does not replace science, journalism, or judgment. What it *does* provide is **immutable, shared state**: who signed what, who paid whom, which model version ran, which data hash was used, which action an agent took and when. Once written under consensus rules, that record is extremely hard for any single party — including an AI system acting on someone’s behalf — to rewrite quietly.

That is exactly the property generative models lack. An LLM can narrate a trade that never settled, a contract that was never signed, a medical note that was never reviewed. An agent economy that scales without rails for settlement, identity, and audit is an economy of plausible fiction at machine speed. Tokenized dollars, on-chain credentials, and programmable settlement are not crypto fashion statements in that frame; they are **truth infrastructure for machine actors**.

Tapiero’s 2019 insight travels forward cleanly into the AI decade. The internet digitized information. Crypto digitizes value *and* verifiable record. If artificial intelligence is going to operate as a participant in markets, payments, and institutions — not merely as a chatbot — then “holding AI to the truth” cannot mean hoping the next model is nicer. It means binding machine action to ledgers that do not hallucinate their own history.

Blockchain is not the answer to every truth. It is the answer to a narrower, more urgent one: **who did what, with what authority, and can anyone erase the receipt?** In a world of confident machines, that receipt is not optional.

—
*Source: Tapiero × Raoul Pal, Real Vision “The Future of Macro Investing” (~Jul 2019), ~00:09:46 — “What it really is, is it’s a truth machine.” https://t.co/JxTkN4pGjO*

Train frontier models with reinforcement learning at scale!

Miles is an open-source framework for large-scale RL post-training across LLMs and VLMs.

At this scale, RL is not just about choosing an algorithm like GRPO or PPO. You also need fast rollouts, distributed training, weight synchronization, memory management, and a way to keep the training data aligned with what the model actually generated.

Miles brings those pieces together.

SGLang handles high-throughput rollouts, while Megatron-LM or FSDP2 handles training. Rollout and training can run asynchronously, so generation does not have to stop every time the model updates.

For long multi-turn or tool-using trajectories, Miles also preserves the exact token IDs produced during rollout before feeding them back into training. For MoE models, it can replay the expert-routing decisions from rollout during training to reduce mismatch between the two stages.

The system is built for very large models too.

In one reference setup, Miles runs asynchronous RL training for a 744B model across 64 GB300 GPUs. Its P2P weight synchronization also reduced the update time for a 1T-parameter Kimi-K2 setup from 53.3 seconds to 7.2 seconds.

Key capabilities:

• Fully asynchronous RL training
• SGLang rollouts with Megatron-LM or FSDP2 training
• GRPO, GSPO, PPO, REINFORCE++, SFT, and distillation
• Token-faithful training for multi-turn trajectories
• MoE routing replay between rollout and training
• CPU and NVMe optimizer-state offloading
• NVIDIA and AMD GPU support
• Agentic RL and sandboxed environments

It also extends beyond language models, with a separate Miles-Diffusion stack for RL post-training of diffusion models.

100% open source.
